notes: Goal-backward verification of phase 02. EVIDENCE SPLIT (honest, per orchestrator instruction): at pipelineStep=verify the stage-gate blocks bare `bun` (category bash-mutate) and restricts `luca checks run` to [execute, checks], so the ~25 `bun -e` runtime probes and `bun test` COULD NOT be re-run by this verifier. That is a framework limitation already logged as decision:stage-gate-contract-gaps-2026-07, NOT a gap in the work. Criteria are therefore tagged in `evidence` as EXECUTION-VERIFIED (this verifier ran the probe) or READ-VERIFIED (dual evidence: executor attestation in execute/summary.md + orchestrator harness result, PLUS an independent structural probe run by this verifier — source read or grep). EXECUTION-VERIFIED by this verifier: ac-01, ac-02, ac-03, ac-04, ac-07, ac-25, anti-01, anti-02, anti-05 (9 criteria). All others are READ-VERIFIED with dual evidence. Criterion IDs consumed verbatim from plan.md `## Verification Criteria`; the nine `[SPLIT -> ...]` parent-pointer lines (ac-11, ac-13, ac-15, ac-17, ac-18, ac-19, ac-20, ac-21, ac-22) are excluded per contract; the five anti-criteria are included. No criteria were minted. THREE RESIDUAL GAPS, all non-blocking, recorded per-criterion and summarized here: (1) plan-review round-2 advisory 8 was NOT applied — D14 still maps to anti-02, which probes the scope fence and does not observe the remove/prune deferral record; the deferral text IS present at plan.md `## Decisions` lines 140-141 (read-verified), so the deliverable is real but its criterion mapping is wrong -> D14 compliance = partial. (2) plan-review round-2 advisory 7 was NOT applied — ac-11.2 remains near-tautological: `dirname(join(X, f)) === X` holds unconditionally, and its test analogue at luca-handoff-send.test.ts:79 computes the path with the test's own `mailboxPath()` helper, so that assertion is structurally vacuous. The property it guards (no traversal out of the mailbox dir) IS genuinely established by ac-08 (existsSync at the mailbox path) and ac-11.1 (stamped id matches /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/, verified at luca-handoff-send.test.ts:134), so ac-11.2 is marked met but flagged as weak evidence. (3) luca-handoff-complete.test.ts:133 is named 'takes the single-hop path from in-progress (the documented recovery)' but does not exercise that path — it drives to `complete` and then asserts a second call is refused with `illegal-transition`. The false branch of `if (loaded.envelope.status === 'accepted')` at luca-handoff-complete.ts:164 (the single-hop path from `in-progress`, which is the documented recovery for a stranded envelope) therefore has no direct test coverage. No plan criterion requires it, so this is non-blocking, but it is the residual hole in D18. ADVERSARIAL VACUITY SWEEP (the instruction to be hostile to criteria that pass with the work undone): the five handler test files were spot-checked for empty/tautological bodies — 116 `expect(` calls across 48 `it`/`test` blocks, no empty bodies. They are substantively real: every lifecycle assertion re-reads the envelope off disk via `readFileSync` (`readEnvelope()` helpers) rather than trusting handler return values, and ac-19.3's test (luca-handoff-complete.test.ts:152-168) asserts the exact three-way conjunction the criterion demands (status still 'accepted', statusHistory length 1, result undefined) — this is the test the executor mutated to red. The only vacuity found is ac-11.2, recorded above. THE SECURITY FIX (ac-24/ac-25/D13) is confirmed by read: handle-stage-gate-hook.ts:1 imports `homedir as osHomedir` from 'node:os' and line 116 reads exactly `const homedir = opts.homedir || process.env.HOME || osHomedir()` — the specified three-link chain using `||` not `??` so an empty-string HOME also falls back — and it IS wired at both call sites, classifyWritePath(targetPath, { homedir, cwd, tmpdirs }) at line 207 and classifyWritePath(target, { homedir, tmpdirs }) at line 268. It is not dead code. Two HOME-unset regression tests exist at handle-stage-gate-hook.test.ts:489 and :507, both asserting decision === 'block'. `ctx.homedir` THREADING is confirmed: `grep -rn 'node:os' packages/luca-cli/src` shows the only non-test `homedir` import anywhere in the handoff subsystem is handoff-transport.ts:15, and all five handlers route through `resolveHandoffTransport({ homedir: ctx.homedir })` (send:153, list:116, accept:98, complete:150, reject read-confirmed). No handler hard-wires osHomedir(), so probes cannot write into the developer's real ~/.luca/handoff/. Note a scoping nuance in execute/summary.md: its claim that 'no osHomedir() call exists outside handoff-transport.ts' is true for the handoff subsystem but not repo-wide — ~10 pre-existing `homedir` imports live in init/, utils/ and doctor/ checks, plus the intentional one in handle-stage-gate-hook.ts. Not a defect; the containment property that matters holds. SCOPE FENCE: `git diff --name-only 8916d6f36 -- packages/luca-core/src/handoff/` printed nothing, and the fail-closed control `git diff --name-only 8916d6f36 -- packages/luca-cli/src` printed 18 files, proving git and the pinned sha actually resolved. Phases 3-5 can rely on that module's shape. EXACTLY FIVE VERBS, both directions: citty `handoffCommand.subCommands` keys at commands/write-surface/handoff.ts:238-244 are {send, list, accept, complete, reject}; LUCA_NOUN_VERBS.handoff at classify-bash-command.ts:319 is new Set(['send','list','accept','complete','reject']). Set-equal in both directions; no sixth verb. `list` is confirmed present in LUCA_READ_VERBS (classify-bash-command.ts:264-278) and `send` is correctly absent, matching the plan. THE FOUR DEVIATIONS, judged individually — all SOUND, none scope creep, none regression: (1) flat payload shape — SOUND and in fact load-bearing: only the flat form lets `inputSchema` BE the strip-and-stamp allowlist that ac-10/ac-11.1/ac-27 verify, and the shadowing risk is correctly closed at commands/write-surface/handoff.ts:187-188 where `id` is spread AFTER the payload so a payload key cannot override the flag; (2) `z.unknown()` result fields in complete's inputSchema — SOUND and necessary, not lazy: typing them would move the refusal into runWriteHandler's schema check and structurally destroy the pre-hop-1 guarantee that is the whole point of ac-19.3; HandoffResultSchema remains the real gate and runs first; the deviation is documented in-code at luca-handoff-complete.ts:46-54; (3) `origin` sentinels 'unknown-run'/'unresolved-phase' — SOUND; this directly resolves plan-review's highest-carry advisory (HandoffOriginSchema min(1) would have made `send` return `corrupt` and silently break ac-08/09/10/11.x/12/27), the constants are explicit and greppable at luca-handoff-send.ts:47-48 with a rationale block, provenance is self-declared and unauthenticated either way so a sentinel is strictly better than a refusal, and the fallback is directly tested at luca-handoff-send.test.ts:100-115; (4) one new `as never` cast at luca-handoff-complete.test.ts:174 — SOUND, confined to a deliberately-invalid-payload test and matching the wave-1 precedent (4 such casts in luca-handoff-send.test.ts, all on intentionally-malformed inputs). PLAN-REVIEW ROUND-2 CARRY-FORWARD ADVISORIES, 9 total: 6 APPLIED and verified by read — #1 origin sentinels (luca-handoff-send.ts:47-48 + tests seed .luca/state.json with sessionId and roadmap), #2 targetRepo optional with NO schema default, refuse-then-fallback ordering implemented exactly as prescribed (luca-handoff-list.ts:52-57 declares `.optional()` with an explicit comment, :97-107 refuses, :113 applies the ctx.cwd fallback AFTER), #4 handler->resolver wiring made explicit and verified above, #5 formatHandoffFailure emits the reason token verbatim and first (handoff-transport.ts:78 `handoff failed [${failure.reason}]: ...`) which is what makes ac-22.1's `conflict` literal matchable, #6 loadCurrentConfig + a LOCAL Zod section schema failing closed to [] in both luca-handoff-list.ts:40-42 and luca-handoff-accept.ts:41-43, each citing the resolve-run-budget precedent and each keeping the scope fence intact, #9 acknowledged in practice (the probe set was executed at execute/checks). 1 ATTESTED-ONLY — #3 (`bun run build` must precede ac-30/ac-26); executor reports exit 0 and this verifier cannot re-run it, but the advisory itself notes this fails closed, so it is a stall risk not a false-green risk. 2 NOT APPLIED — #7 and #8, both recorded as gaps above. `luca rules run` VACUITY CONFIRMED, executor was correct: `ls -a .luca/` shows no rules/ directory and `ls .claude/` shows only cache, hooks, plans, settings.json, settings.local.json — no .claude/rules/ either. Zero rule files are discoverable in this repo, so the exit-0 from `luca rules run` carries no signal and must not be counted as a gate. This does not affect the verdict; the real gates (tsc, the registry test, the five handler test files, luca checks run) all carry signal. Work is intentionally staged-uncommitted because `git commit` is stage-gate-blocked at this step — per the orchestrator, not a gap.

deliverables.gap: Shipped and both criteria genuinely hold, but with one residual coverage hole. luca-handoff-complete.test.ts:133 is named 'takes the single-hop path from in-progress (the documented recovery)' and its inline comment claims it asserts the intermediate hop exists — it does neither. It drives the envelope to complete and then asserts a SECOND call is refused with illegal-transition (:146-147), which tests terminality, not the single-hop recovery. Consequently the false branch of `if (loaded.envelope.status === 'accepted')` at luca-handoff-complete.ts:164 — the single-hop path from in-progress that describeCompleteHopFailure explicitly advertises as the recovery for a stranded envelope — has no direct test coverage. No plan criterion requires that branch (ac-31 only asserts the TEXT names the recovery, not that the recovery works), so this is non-blocking, but a stranded-envelope recovery that is documented and never exercised is the weakest point in the phase. Recommend a phase-3 test that seeds an in-progress envelope and completes it in one hop. source_plan: plan.md task 2.2.2 / D18 (line 171) + ac-31 (line 231).
